recap.label: Daily Recap
recap.periodEnd: Mon, Nov 16, 2026, 4:00 PM ET (that day's close)
recap.timezoneNote: All times below are shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, stocks slid sharply, with the S&P 500 recording a third straight decline and its biggest loss since Nvidia's chief resigned last week (5:06 PM ET). The Financial Times reported the Nasdaq 100 sank 2.7% as US chip stocks fell and Nvidia sustained a fresh bout of selling pressure ahead of its earnings (4:58 PM ET). MarketWatch reported Micron, AMD and other AI stocks fell as the chip-sector selloff intensified, with investors jittery about Nvidia's earnings and whether it will scale back financing of the AI ecosystem (4:17 PM ET), and that the Commerce Department announced a rule aimed at restricting China's remote access to advanced chips (4:53 PM ET). WSJ reported Treasury yields declined as Fed Chairman Warsh refrained from giving hints about the path of interest rates (3:47 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

cryptoDriver.text: CoinDesk reported bitcoin slipped after rebounding from a low that triggered $2 billion of liquidations over the weekend (6:03 AM ET). WSJ reported crypto started the week on a downbeat note, with both Bitcoin and Ethereum trading around key support levels as risk appetite remains constrained (4:05 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

items.headline: Nvidia's Board Not Considering Reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
items.summary: Per WSJ, billionaire allies have called for his return as inquiries into his relationship with a woman suspected of working with Chinese intelligence proceed. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's stock extends decline following harsh words from the U.S. government
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, the Commerce Department announced a new rule aimed at restricting China's remote access to advanced chips. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Short Sellers Reap $24 Billion as Stock Extends Slide
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's tumble in the wake of the scandal that led to former CEO Jensen Huang's ouster has fueled tens of billions of dollars in gains for short sellers. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Singapore agrees to continue discussions with US on Megaspeed case
items.summary: Per South China Morning Post, Singapore's government said on Monday it had agreed to continue discussions with the United States about Megaspeed, the company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI 'National Champions'
items.summary: Per WSJ, the new program is part of an effort to help U.S. AI companies compete for business overseas. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
items.summary: Per WSJ, interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals after a stretch in which Nvidia aggressively financed computing deals and startup investments. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Bessent Urges Nvidia to Pick Outsider as Next CEO
items.summary: Per WSJ, the Treasury Secretary questioned whether the chip maker pushed illicit China sales to boost revenue. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: The Campaign to Bring Back Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
items.summary: Per WSJ, in open letters, phone calls and group chats, Huang's allies are making the case that his ouster was hasty, even as legal scrutiny intensifies. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

morning.label: Morning Brief
morning.timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary. The overnight news snapshot for this morning was not available for this run, so coverage runs through about 9:04 PM ET on Nov 17.

driver.text: Per WSJ, US stocks finished lower on Tuesday as doubts about the sustainability of the AI boom festered ahead of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's market debut (5:07 PM ET). Per Bloomberg, a rebound fueled by Nvidia's better-than-expected sales forecast lost momentum as traders stayed wary of the AI trade (5:07 PM ET), and gold fell below $3,800 an ounce after Federal Reserve officials made the case for more rate hikes (6:33 PM ET). Per WSJ, Japanese stocks rose 1.0% led by chip and AI shares after Nvidia's results eased fears about the AI trade (7:34 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

calendar.text: Anthropic's market debut is expected, per WSJ.
A slate of Federal Reserve speeches and the central bank's most recent meeting minutes are due, per Bloomberg.

items.summary: In an 8-K (Items 2.02 and 9.01) accepted Nov 17 at 4:20 PM ET, NVIDIA furnished its press release on results for the quarter ended October 25, 2026, CFO commentary from Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress, and supplemental financial information. items.headline: Nvidia Reports Faster Growth, Says Jensen Huang Won't Return as CEO
items.summary: Per WSJ, in her first earnings call as interim CEO, Colette Kress faced questions over the chipmaker's future without its longtime leader. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia results beat expectations, as ousted CEO Huang told no way back
items.summary: Per South China Morning Post, Nvidia doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than US$115 billion, the company reported on Tuesday while ruling out any return for ousted CEO Jensen Huang. Written from the headline and the publisher's opening summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's stock rises as blowout numbers help ease CEO transition fears
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, Nvidia's revenue growth and $130 billion quarterly forecast showed that demand for chips is still sky-high. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Stops Selling AI Chips to China Despite US Approval
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia is no longer shipping Hopper data center chips to China, despite winning the US government's blessing to sell a version of that model to the Asian country. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: The SEC Is Investigating Nvidia
items.summary: Per WSJ, the SEC is investigating Nvidia. Written from the headline only.

items.headline: Nvidia Does Not Intend to Bring Back Huang as CEO, Chair Says
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board, says former CEO Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned and the board does not intend to rehire him, speaking on the earnings call. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Microsoft Executive Says Nvidia Drama Could Boost Rival Chips
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's corporate drama could help prompt customers to consider alternatives to the company's AI chips, according to a top Microsoft executive. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.
